'''Britta Siegers''' (born 4 July 1966) is a retired [[German people|German]] [[wheelchair tennis]] player and [[Paralympic swimming|Paralympic swimmer]] who competed in international level events. She was the first German disabled athlete to compete in two different sports at the [[Paralympics]]: she was a swimmer from [[1984 Summer Paralympics|1984]] to [[1992 Summer Paralympics|1992]] and returned twelve years later as a wheelchair tennis player at the [[2004 Summer Paralympics]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=7 May 2012|title=News from JTFP (in German)|url=https://www.dbs-npc.de/dbsj-nachrichten-jtfp/weltklasse-athletin-britta-siegers-setzt-hoffnung-in-jtfp.html|url-status=live|access-date=|website=Deutsche Behindertensport Jugend|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017214856/https://www.dbs-npc.de/dbsj-nachrichten-jtfp/weltklasse-athletin-britta-siegers-setzt-hoffnung-in-jtfp.html |archive-date=2020-10-17 }}</ref>

==Swimming career==
Siegers' first sport was swimming when she started in 1969 after she lost both of her legs in a train accident aged two years old. She swam competitively in 1984 at the Summer Paralympics and won her first medals there. Her most successful Paralympic Games was in 1992 where she won five gold medals, two silvers and one bronze medal, she narrowly missed winning her consecutive [[freestyle swimming|freestyle]] titles after being beaten by [[Priya Cooper]] in both the 50m and 100m freestyle S8.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=12 October 2020|title=Britta Siegers - IPC Profile|url=https://www.paralympic.org/britta-siegers|url-status=live|access-date=|website=International Paralympic Committee|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201012132621/https://www.paralympic.org/britta-siegers |archive-date=2020-10-12 }}</ref>

==Tennis career==
Siegers began playing wheelchair tennis in the early 1994 after her retirement to swimming in 1992. She won seven singles titles and eleven doubles titles and her highest ranking was World No. 8 in July 2003, she competed at her fourth and last Summer Paralympics Games in [[Athens]] in 2004 where she reached the quarterfinals in the [[Wheelchair tennis at the 2004 Summer Paralympics - Women's Singles|women's singles]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=12 October 2020|title=Britta Siegers - ITF Profile|url=https://www.itftennis.com/en/players/britta-siegers/800198518/ger/wct/s/overview/#pprofile-info-tabs|archive-date=|access-date=|website=International Tennis Federations}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=3 June 2004|title=The second career of the power woman (in German)|url=https://www.ksta.de/die-zweite-karriere-der-powerfrau-14308596|archive-date=|access-date=|website=ksta.de}}</ref>
